items.title: Stock market holiday today: Are NSE, BSE closed for Gandhi Jayanti? Check 2026 holiday list
items.description: Indian stock markets will remain closed on October 2 for Gandhi Jayanti, with trading resuming next week. MCX and NCDEX will also remain shut. The market holiday comes after the Sensex and Nifty extended losses on Thursday, weighed down by rising bond yields, elevated crude prices and broad-based selling pressure.

items.title: ​Coal India, NTPC among 360 ONE Capital’s 8 stock picks for October. Check full list with target prices
items.description: 360 ONE Capital Research has identified eight stocks as its top picks in its October 2026 portfolio update. The list includes Coal India, NTPC, ITC and five other stocks, with the brokerage outlining its target prices and key factors supporting each Buy recommendation.

items.title: Bajaj Finance to raise Rs 17,500 cr via QIP, pref issue
items.description: Bajaj Finance plans to raise up to Rs 17,500 crore through a Rs 11,700-crore QIP and Rs 5,800 crore warrant issue to promoter Bajaj Finserv. The fundraising requires shareholder approval; institutional investors will receive QIP shares while promoter warrants could help maintain Bajaj Finserv’s stake and limit dilution.

items.title: Jefferies is bullish on 6 healthcare stocks with upside potential of up to 46%. Own any?
items.description: Hospital stocks including Fortis Healthcare, Dr Agarwal’s, Manipal, Apollo Hospitals and Medanta extended their losses for a second straight session on Thursday, after falling as much as 10% in the previous session, as the Supreme Court questioned steep markups on cancer drugs and asked the government to examine allegations that hospitals require patients to purchase medicines from their own or designated pharmacies. However, Jefferies sees this as an excellent entry point to buy these 6 stocks.

items.title: Market crash wipes out Rs 26 lakh cr in 8 weeks! Why soaring bond yields may hurt Sensex, Nifty more than elevated oil prices
items.description: The Sensex and Nifty have fallen for eight straight weeks, wiping out more than Rs 26 lakh crore in market capitalisation. While elevated oil prices have pressured equities, soaring bond yields, foreign outflows, a stronger dollar and tighter liquidity are adding to the selling pressure and weighing on investor sentiment.

items.title: D-Street logs longest spell of week slump in 25 years
items.description: Indian equity markets faced significant pressure as US bond yields surged, leading to a record selloff. The Sensex and Nifty experienced prolonged declines, surpassing previous downturns witnessed during the Covid pandemic. Foreign investors continued to withdraw their investments amidst rising crude oil prices, negatively impacting the rupee's value. Analysts suggest selective stock opportunities may arise despite challenging macroeconomic conditions.

items.title: Sri Lotus shares rally 29% in a month. Can luxury and redevelopment sustain the momentum?
items.description: Sri Lotus Developers & Realty has seen a remarkable 29% increase in shares, significantly outpacing the wider market. This boost is attributed to the anticipation surrounding their luxury initiatives and redevelopment projects, which promise robust pre-sales and profit margins. With 22 projects planned, the anticipated gross development value ranges from ₹17,500 to ₹18,000 crore. Furthermore, collections have surged year-over-year, suggesting a bright growth trajectory for the current fiscal year.

items.title: FPIs pull record Rs 3 lakh crore from Indian equities in 9 months. More pain ahead?
items.description: In an unprecedented turn of events, foreign portfolio investors have divested a staggering amount exceeding ₹3 lakh crore from Indian equities within the initial nine months of 2026. This marks a record outflow, largely driven by rising US bond yields and ongoing geopolitical conflicts, which diminish India's appeal for international investors.

items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 33% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: In its latest downturn phase, the market has been falling for close to a month-and-a-half, with only the occasional bounce. In a stretch like this, you may get a sharp upmove caused by short covering, where traders who had bet on a fall buy back to close their positions, pushing prices up for a while. Do not mistake such a bounce for an end to the current troubles.

items.title: Sebi penalises SMC Global Securities for compliance lapses
items.description: Sebi has levied a penalty of Rs 1 lakh on SMC Global Securities due to regulatory infractions, particularly the mishandling of client order-placement records uncovered during an inspection. This examination, covering the period from January to September 2024, highlighted issues tied to unauthorized trading and the oversight of authorized representative Amit Lilhare's client transactions. SMC Global Securities operates under Sebi’s regulations and engages with various stock exchanges across India.

items.title: FPIs turn net sellers, pull out Rs 35,860 cr in Sep
items.description: In September, foreign portfolio investors shed a staggering Rs 35,860 crore from Indian equities, driven by global uncertainties and rising US interest rates. This selling trend persisted into October with an outflow of Rs 9,232 crore. This selling follows significant investments of Rs 49,830 crore made in July and August.

items.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: Decoding the new investment landscape and shift in smart money
items.description: Transformations in the global economy are reshaping how investors allocate capital and devise strategies. Geopolitical conflicts and tech rivalries are challenging conventional wisdom, leading to heightened interest in markets such as India, Southeast Asia, and the Gulf states. Strategic investments in infrastructure and commodities have gained importance. The upcoming ET Alpha Wealth Summit aims to delve into these transformative investment trends.
